To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) cellular-enabled water sensors can be deployed to monitor handpump functionality in remote rural settings; (b) sensor data can be used to dispatch technicians, improving functionality; (c) the cost per functional water point per year is comparable between the three service delivery models; and (d) the benefits of reliable service delivery may justify greater focus of resources on servicing models over new installation models.

1) the "ambulance" approach of dispatching technicians based on sensor data was the most successful model in terms of time to repair, and 2) the cost per functional handpump per year was similar between the models.
the ambulance service model is more responsive than the nominal and circuit rider models, but is also more costly, and the nominal maintenance model is the most cost-effective model.

the question of how to improve the maintenance service delivery model for handpumps in sub-Saharan Africa.
